subject: Dedicated capacity playbook - OptiLabs GA sizing and surge policy
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@optilabs.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 09 Feb 2027 09:12:03 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity planning for OptiLabs GA - traffic samples attached

Hi Aisha / Ben,

Thanks for taking this on. We’re planning an aggressive GA for OptiLabs in Q2 and need a dedicated capacity proposal we can take to procurement and infra. High level:

- Monthly token volume (estimate): ~2.2B tokens
- Expected steady-state peak (business hours): ~30,000 tokens/sec sustained for 2–4 hours/day
- Burst windows: up to ~90,000 tokens/sec for 10–15 minute windows (marketing-driven spikes)
- Workload mix: ~65% chat (assistant-style, multi-turn), 35% batch/aux requests; average tokens per request ~450 (input ~80 / output ~370)
- SLO targets: p95 end-to-end latency <= 300ms; p99 <= 600ms; availability goal 99.9%

We need: an initial GPU-count recommendation (H100-equivalent), a suggested baseline vs burst pool sizing, recommended model variants (perf vs cost-optimized), and a fallback strategy to keep the product within SLOs during bursts.

Attached is a 48-hour traffic sample and a short note on traffic shaping rules (OptiLabs_prod_traffic_sample.csv). Please let us know what additional traces you need. Ideally we can get a proposal/ballpark by end of day tomorrow so we can align with procurement.

Best,
Laura

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning for OptiLabs GA - traffic samples attached

Thanks Laura — great context. I did a quick run of Redwood’s bench numbers against the traffic profile you sent. Below are two realistic sizing options plus a short set of assumptions. This is a working draft; we’ll refine with raw token-level traces if you can share them.

Assumptions (short):
- Avg request size: 450 tokens (per your note). Sequence length distribution centered ~350–500 tokens.
- Benchmarks run on H100-80GB equivalence with typical batching and KV cache behavior.
- Cache hit rate: assumed 0–12% for multi-turn warm prefixes (we’ll refine with traces).
- Target SLO mapping: p95 <= 300ms; p99 <= 600ms.

Option A — Performance-first (FP16, lower latency):
- Model: redwood-realtime-13B-fp16 (baseline, better single-stream latency)
- Measured throughput (avg, seq~450, batch 8): ~620 tokens/sec per H100-eq GPU
- Recommended baseline (sustained 30k tok/s): ceil(30000 / 620) = 49 GPUs (reserve)
- Burst capacity for 90k tok/s: ceil(90000 / 620) = 146 GPUs (allocate as burst pool + autoscale)
- Suggested baseline + burst approach: reserve 50 GPUs, burst pool up to additional 110 GPUs (total ephemeral max ~160) to cover spikes while keeping baseline costs predictable

Option B — Cost-optimized (Quantized variant):
- Model: redwood-13B-q4f (quantized, better throughput at slight quality delta)
- Measured throughput (avg, seq~450, batch 8): ~970 tokens/sec per H100-eq GPU
- Recommended baseline (sustained 30k tok/s): ceil(30000 / 970) = 31 GPUs (reserve)
- Burst capacity for 90k tok/s: ceil(90000 / 970) = 93 GPUs
- Suggested baseline + burst approach: reserve 32 GPUs, burst pool up to 70 GPUs (target total ~100)

Headroom recommendation: we typically add ~20–40% headroom to baseline for operational events and maintenance. For OptiLabs I recommend reserving the quantized baseline (Option B) for cost reasons with a larger burst pool, but keeping a small FP16 reserve for latency-critical endpoints (canary / high-priority customers).

Next steps I need from you to finalize:
1) A rolling 7–14 day token-level trace (timestamped per request, token count, request type)
2) Confirmation of which endpoints must meet p95=300ms vs which can tolerate p95=500ms (we can optimize per-route)
3) Any regulatory constraints that require on-prem or VPC-only nodes (affects placement and burst sizing)

I attached a starter sizing workbook with the math so you can tweak assumptions (optilabs_initial_sizing_table.xlsx). If that looks ok I’ll loop Jonas for a runbook / autoscale thresholds + fallback plan.

Thanks —
Aisha Rahman

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning for OptiLabs GA - traffic samples attached

Thanks all — dug into the sample and ran a short queue simulation against our latency model. A few actionable details and a suggested runbook below.

Key simulation inputs (from sample + assumptions):
- Peak envelope: 90k tok/s for 10–15m windows; steady 30k tok/s during business hours
- Avg sequence: 450 tokens; batch strategy: continuous batching with max batch size 12 for chat; we modeled KV cache warmup with an optimistic 12% hit rate
- Model choices analyzed: redwood-13B-q4f (primary), redwood-realtime-13B-fp16 (fallback for latency-sensitive routes)

Simulated outcomes (single-region, H100-eq fleet):
- Quantized baseline (32 reserved GPUs) + burst pool (64 GPUs) + 12% cache hit: predicted p95 ~= 280–320ms (depends on exact request fan-out), p99 ~= 520–620ms during sustained peak.
- FP16 baseline (50 reserved GPUs) + burst pool (110 GPUs): predicted p95 ~= 240–290ms, p99 ~= 480–580ms, but materially higher monthly cost.

Recommended operational design (middle-ground):
1) Reserve 40 H100-equivalent GPUs running redwood-13B-q4f (covers steady-state with ~20% operational headroom after accounting for node maintenance/faults).
2) Configure burst pool up to +60 GPUs (autoscale with aggressive pre-warming heuristics for marketing spikes). This yields net capacity ~100 GPUs on extreme bursts and gets us within p95=300ms for most scenarios in sim.
3) Hot fallback: keep 6 FP16 instances (redwood-realtime-13B-fp16) pinned to serve a prioritized route (enterprise customers) to ensure sub-300ms tails for premium users.
4) Autoscale & pre-warm policy: trigger pre-warm when queue depth exceeds 750 requests OR when 5-minute average token rate exceeds 70% of baseline. Pre-warm target: 10–20 GPUs in <5m.
5) Cache & batching recommendations: enable KV prefix warming for returning sessions, set batching window to 20ms for chat endpoints to balance latency/throughput.
6) Fallback plan: under overload, automatically redirect ~20% of requests to the quantized-compact model with a transparent hint to clients. If p99 breach persists > 2m, escalate to throttling low-priority routes and send rate-limit headers (429) with retry-after.

Operational runbook items to include for procurement and SRE:
- Incidents: checklist for adding burst capacity, diagnosing cold-cache tail latency, and model-fallback toggles (Doc IDs included in runbook).
- Cost model: baseline commit (40 GPUs, quantized) + burst invoice (per-GPU minute billing) with estimated monthly spend at current token volumes (we’ll provide exact numbers once you confirm commit).
- Validation plan: 14-day canary (8–12 reserved GPUs) with synthetic spike tests to validate pre-warm and cache hit improvements.

I’ve attached a short runbook with the autoscale thresholds and the simulation charts (optilabs_runbook_v1.pdf). If you want we can schedule a 30-min SRE handoff to walk the playbook and run the synthetic tests next week.
